Resolves #16435

⚖️ A Workstation tab hidden for six minutes now hands its own size changes to the App Worker in 0.71 s. On the branch point, the same change had still not arrived 90 s later.

## What was slow, measured

The ResizeObserver addon's hidden poll and the timer arm of its dispatch dam are main-thread timers, and a hidden page can hold those to one wake per minute. A size change waited for the next minute-aligned poll pass, then for the timer arm. A worker's timer and its message to the page are not throttled: #16435 measured 120 of 120 messages arriving within 1 ms, in a page whose own interval ticked 2 of 120 times.

## The change

| | |
|---|---|
| `worker.HiddenTick` (new) | The App Worker sends each hidden window a `hiddenTick` once per second |
| `worker.App` | Starts and stops the tick from `visibilityChange`, and at connect from `getWindowData`, which now reports `hidden` — a window that loads in the background never reports a flip |
| `main.addon.ResizeObserver` | Polls on each tick. A hidden document dispatches at once instead of waiting on either dam arm; the interval stays as the floor for a window nobody ticks |

| AC-1 | Ticked on the ticket before this PR, on the pre-repair in-situ receipt |

| AC-3 | `WorkstationStarvedGeometryNL` and its sibling `WorkstationStarvedTourNL` **pass** at `546029404d`, and both pass at the branch point. The visible path runs the same code as before: while `document.hidden` is false, `armDispatch` races rAF against the timer exactly as it did |
| AC-4 | The addon's class doc names the hidden layer's carrier. `DockFlip`'s cross-reference, *"paint-gated carriers need a paint-independent arm"*, is now true of both addons, so it stays as written |

**AC-2.** One probe, one stimulus: the page's own dedicated worker changes `.neo-viewport`'s width at 1 and 6 minutes hidden, so nothing outside the page wakes it. Each tree was served by `webpack serve` from its own worktree. Chrome ran headless, and the three throttling-disable flags were verified absent.

| hidden for | branch point `d688710175` | carrier `45b50bad88` |
|---|---|---|

| 6 min | **not delivered by the read at 7.5 min**: the one-minute poll detected it after 48.0 s, and the timer arm was still waiting | **0.71 s** |

## Deltas from ticket

- **The tick does not check `isWindowDeparted()`**, although the design note on the ticket named that check. `removePort()` marks a window departed whenever one of its ports retires, even while another port for that window remains, so the check would silence a live window. A departed window has no port, and a tick that resolves none already stops. A unit arm pins it.
- **A window that connects hidden is ticked from connect.** The design note did not cover this. No boot-time visibility report exists, so a tab loaded in the background would otherwise wait for a flip that never comes.
- **Tick and interval run side by side, uncoordinated.** I wrote a stand-down for the interval and removed it: a redundant pass compares against `#lastDispatchedSize`, so it dispatches nothing.
- **Both starved specs' closing rig control changed.** They proved the rig by counting the app's frame requests. Those requests came from `armDispatch` arming rAF while hidden, which is exactly what this PR removes. So at `fea3f4e879` both closing controls went red while every leg before them passed, and the branch point stayed green. The controls now witness the rig directly: targets were observed through the silent stub, and `requestAnimationFrame` is still the black hole at the end.

## Bounds

- Occluded-but-visible windows are unchanged, which is the ticket's named residual.
- **A busy App Worker delays the tick along with everything else.** Every instrumented run showed one 18–40 s stretch where the Workstation App Worker handled nothing. It appeared on the branch point as much as on the carrier, and in a tab that never hid. A CPU profile puts it in `grid.Container#onResize` → `Body#createRowPool`: row registrations log *"Trying to create an item with an already existing id"*, and each log is mirrored through `ai.Client#sendNotification` over its WebSocket (12 of 39 busy seconds). Its trigger is not isolated. No carrier can get geometry to a worker that is not handling events, so this is recorded on #16435 rather than fixed here.
- Every hidden window gets one tick per second for as long as it stays hidden, whether or not anything on it observes size.
- Measured in Google Chrome only.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] Re-run the AC-2 probe route recorded on #16435 against `dev`, and post the receipt on the ticket. I will do this myself. No CI tier can re-witness it: every whitebox e2e profile launches with the throttling-disable flags under Playwright's focus emulation, so none of them ever sees a hidden document.

Evidence: **L2** (before/after on a real hidden Chrome tab, from the branch point and the carrier; the two whitebox e2e specs the ticket names, with the branch point as control; full unit tier) → L2 required. Residual: the App Worker busy periods above, recorded on #16435.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge:**

**The one wired path with no arm is the one the design note did not cover.** Everything else in this diff is pinned: `sync` lifecycle, tick routing, dam bypass, visible-document no-op, destroy-unsubscribes. The connect-hidden path — `Main#getWindowData` now reporting `hidden`, `App#onConnect` feeding it to `sync` — is asserted nowhere. I verified its placement is right (after **both** `isCurrentPort` guards, before `fire('connect')`), and I verified it degrades safely: a `getWindowData` rejection leaves `windowData` undefined and `windowData &&` skips the call, while a `hidden` that arrives `undefined` takes `sync`'s `!hidden` branch into a `stop()` on a window that has no timer — a no-op. So this is not a defect claim.

It is a coverage asymmetry worth naming, because the failure it guards is the silent-forever one: a tab that loads in the background never flips, so if this wire ever breaks, nothing reports it — the window simply keeps its old geometry until someone looks at it. The `HiddenTick` spec already builds a worker stub; an `App#onConnect` arm feeding `{hidden: true}` through it is cheap. Not blocking, and not a required action — your call whether it lands here or as a follow-up.

**Follow-up concern (non-blocking, and already half-declared in your Bounds):** the tick is unconditional on whether the ticked window has any resize targets, while the information that would gate it (`#targetToComponents` non-empty, which `syncPollState` already computes) lives on the other side of the boundary. Today that is one message per second per hidden window and you have said so. The shape that would retire it is the consumer subscribing rather than the worker broadcasting — at which point `stop()` is driven by the consumer instead of by a failed port lookup. I am recording it as a scaling observation, not asking for it: the current shape is correct, bounded, and the one-consumer case does not earn the protocol yet. `hypothesis — needs V-B-A before implementation`.

That reasoning was correct and is exactly what stops holding once the document is hidden — there is no vsync to align to. This PR does not revoke it; it adds the branch where the premise lapses. Both halves belong in the KB together.
*   **`[TOOLING_GAP]`**: Recorded on your behalf, since it is the reason AC-2 has no CI twin: every whitebox e2e profile launches under Playwright's focus emulation plus the throttling-disable flags, so **no** whitebox run in this repository can observe a hidden document, by construction. Together those are a harness gap with a known workaround and no automation — worth a ticket independent of this PR.
*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: The durable lesson is the control replacement, not the carrier. Both starved e2e rigs closed by counting the app's own frame requests — and those requests came from `armDispatch` arming rAF while hidden, i.e. from the defect. The fix therefore *had* to red its own controls, and the wrong move (relax the assertion) and the right one (witness the rig directly) are indistinguishable in a diff summary. Actively probing `requestAnimationFrame` at the end and asserting the counter moved is strictly stronger than reading a count the app happened to produce: it fails if the stub was ever replaced, which the old form could not detect. **A control that measures a side effect of the bug dies with the bug; a control that probes the rig outlives it.**
